meta.title: Machined parts: quality flow
meta.description: How a machined part moves from supplier intake to dispatch, where it is inspected and what happens to defects. Defect rates in the Defects tab are illustrative.

summary.headline: Quality is checked at intake, after machining and before dispatch; failed parts are reworked once or scrapped, never shipped.
points: Incoming material is checked against its certificate before it enters production
Every batch is measured after machining against the drawing tolerances
Reworked parts are re-inspected like new parts
Packaging includes a final visual check and batch labels for traceability

facts.Traceability: Batch number from raw material to customer

data.title: Supplier intake
data.subtitle: Bar stock and certificates
data.description: Raw material arrives with a material certificate. A sample is checked for dimensions and grade before release to production.

data.title: CNC machining
data.subtitle: Turning and milling
data.description: Parts are cut to the drawing. The operator checks the first part of each batch before running the rest.

data.title: Inspection
data.subtitle: Measure against drawing
data.description: Critical dimensions are measured on a coordinate measuring machine (CMM); surface finish is checked by gauge and eye.

data.title: Rework
data.subtitle: One correction attempt
data.description: Parts with oversize features or burrs are corrected and sent back for full re-inspection. Undersize parts cannot be reworked.

data.title: Scrap and root cause
data.subtitle: Quarantine and record
data.description: Scrapped parts are quarantined, logged with the defect type and reviewed weekly for root causes.

data.title: Packaging
data.subtitle: Final check and labels
data.description: Parts are cleaned, protected against corrosion, packed and labelled with the batch number.

data.title: Dispatch
data.subtitle: With conformity certificate
data.description: Shipped with a certificate of conformity and the inspection report for the batch.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Material flows left to right. Inspection splits each batch into pass, rework and scrap. Click a station to see its typical defects.

steps.title: Intake and machining
steps.description: Certified material is released to the CNC cell, where the first part of each batch is checked before the run continues.

steps.title: Inspection
steps.description: Every batch is measured. Passing parts go on to packaging.

steps.title: Rework loop
steps.description: Fixable parts are corrected once and fully re-inspected. A part that fails again is scrapped.

steps.title: Scrap and learn
steps.description: Unfixable parts are quarantined and their defect type recorded for the weekly root-cause review.

steps.title: Pack and dispatch
steps.description: Packed, labelled parts ship with a certificate of conformity, keeping the batch traceable.

blocks.label: Illustrative figures
blocks.body: Rates below are example values for a training diagram, not measurements from a real line.

items.title: Wrong material grade
items.text: Caught by checking the certificate and a hardness test on a sample.

items.title: Bar diameter out of tolerance
items.text: Measured on a sample before release.

items.title: Tool wear drift
items.text: Dimensions creep as the tool wears; prevented by scheduled tool changes.

items.title: Set-up error
items.text: Caught by first-part inspection before the batch runs.

items.title: Measurement error
items.text: Gauges are calibrated on a schedule and checked against a reference part daily.

items.title: Undersize features
items.text: Material cannot be added back, so these parts are scrapped.

items.title: Burrs and oversize features
items.text: Can be corrected once, then re-inspected.

items.title: Corrosion in transit
items.text: Prevented by cleaning and a protective coating before packing.

items.title: Mixed batches
items.text: One batch per carton, labelled before sealing.
